narrative.overview:
Tableside is a dark card room with a real table at its centre. The table is physical: baize
felt lit from the middle, a walnut rail, and chips, cards and dice drawn as objects you could
pick up. The teaching voice is a dealer standing beside you. It speaks through a note on warm
paper that sits next to the hand rather than covering it, so the reason arrives while the
cards are still on the felt. Everything else (navigation, panels, statistics) is quiet chrome
that makes room for the table and the coach.

The mood is **premium · instructional**.

- **Premium** comes from material and restraint. There is one gold, and it marks action, place
  and money. A Fraunces serif sets headlines and the figures that matter, in cream type on
  near-black.
- **Instructional** comes from the paper layer and from numbers that are always legible and
  traceable.

The interface is clean, legible 2D. It never chases a photorealistic 3D felt or casino-floor
spectacle (ADR-0005); "clean" is still never a licence for a spreadsheet.

The layout is phone-first and comfortably dense. A table screen stacks a top bar and phase
stepper, the felt, a status line, a row of equal-width actions, and the chip rack on its rail.
App screens are one column on phones and open to two or three on desktop inside a 1440 frame.
There is no motion today: state changes are instant.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black green canvas (Night Shift Black), cream type, a single gold accent (House Gold).
Felt, rail, chips, cards and dice rendered as tactile objects with their own shadows.
Coach notes on paper with a 4px edge coloured by verdict: Hint Blue, Replay Coral or Good-Call Green.
Fraunces for display and key figures; Inter for everything the player operates.
App surfaces are separated by tonal steps and 1px hairlines. Shadows belong to objects and overlays.
Every tap target meets the platform minimum: 44pt on iOS and the web, 48dp on Android.
On iOS and Android the platform's own tab bar, back bars and sheets carry navigation; the web keeps its App Header.

rules.name: The House Gold Rule
rules.body: Gold means _act here_, _you are here_ or _money_. Use it for the primary action, the current step, the chosen option and the bankroll. Never use it as decoration, and give each view only one gold-filled button.

rules.name: The Paper Is the Coach Rule
rules.body: Paper carries the teaching voice: coach notes, table tips and the landing page's teaching sections. Inside a control, paper marks the one chosen option. Nothing else sits on paper.

rules.name: The Four-Colour Deck Rule
rules.body: Suits are always four colours. Hearts and diamonds never share red; a glance must separate them.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: The felt prints in one opaque ink, Felt Print. Small felt type ranks by size, weight and tracking, never by fading the ink: translucent cream on lit green fails.

rules.name: The Named Literal Rule
rules.body: Screens never carry a raw hex value. Design variables come from `colors`. A design literal gets a name in `surfaces` or `marketing`, or in a game's own map: `felt` for blackjack, `craps`, `live`, `machine` for the video poker cabinet, and baccarat's `palette`.

rules.name: The Serif Counts Rule
rules.body: Fraunces sets headlines and the numbers worth remembering. Everything the player taps, reads mid-hand or types is Inter.

rules.name: The Fixed Felt Rule
rules.body: The felt is a drawing, not a layout: its type is capped at 1.3× so the table keeps its shape at any text size, and everything around the felt (bars, actions, notes) grows instead.

rules.name: The 16 Floor Rule
rules.body: Running body copy is never smaller than 16px; the system sheet sets this as the minimum for older readers. Use 14px and below only for secondary lines, captions and labels.

rules.name: The Lift Has a Reason Rule
rules.body: A shadow means one of two things: this is an object on the table, or this is a layer above the page. If it is neither, it is flat.

rules.name: The Tactile Felt, Quiet Chrome Rule
rules.body: Objects on the table look physical: chips have edge spots and an inlay, and cards have card stock and a hairline edge. Felt is lit from the centre, and these objects carry shadows. The chrome around the table stays flat, hairlined and restrained, so the eye goes to the table and the coach.

dos: **Do** import colours, spacing, radii and type from `@/ui/ds` (`colors`, `space`, `radius`, `type`, `ui()`, `display()`), and name any new design literal in `surfaces`, `marketing` or the game's own palette map.
**Do** keep House Gold to the one primary action, the current step, the chosen option and the bankroll.
**Do** put the coach's voice on Coach Paper with a 4px verdict edge, beside the hand and never covering the cards.
**Do** keep every tap target at least `MIN_TAP` (44pt iOS and web, 48dp Android), using `hitSlop` when the visual is smaller.
**Do** select type weight by face name through `ui()` / `display()`, never `fontWeight`.
**Do** use Hint Blue Light (#7FA8F2) for informational text on dark surfaces and Hint Ink (#2256BD) for hint text on paper.
**Do** open every modal panel with `Sheet`, so Back, the scrim, the grabber and the keyboard behave the same everywhere.
**Do** give text containers a minimum height, never a fixed one, and cap text only through `textScale` where geometry is fixed.
donts: **Don't** put a raw hex value in a screen file.
**Don't** set Hint Blue (#2D6CDF) as text. It reaches only 4.3:1 on Coach Paper and 3.5:1 on Night Panel; use Hint Ink on paper and Hint Blue Light on dark.
**Don't** fade felt type with alpha; use Felt Print.
**Don't** draw the App Header or any web-style global navigation on iOS or Android.
**Don't** grey out or hide a legal player action to steer the player. Disabled styling is only for actions that are genuinely unavailable.
**Don't** render a photorealistic 3D felt or casino-floor spectacle. The table is clean, legible 2D.
**Don't** add shadows to in-flow panels, stat cards or list rows.
**Don't** use gold as decoration, or put two gold-filled buttons in one view.
